topics.label: geopolitical and security developments
topics.description: A concrete international development with a material economic or market channel established by the reporting: sanctions changing trade or energy exports, disruption or reopening of strategic commercial shipping routes, damage to energy production, or a major war escalation or signed peace agreement with clearly identified economic or supply consequences. A stock-market reaction is not required, but routine battlefield updates, weapons deliveries, military flights or deployments, intelligence sharing, planned diplomatic meetings, official rhetoric and incremental Ukraine, Iran or Taiwan updates without that economic evidence are off-topic. Not historical explainers, generic geopolitical commentary or unsubstantiated rumors.

topics.label: source-reported options flow
topics.description: Reporting of specific observed options transactions or positioning with quantified evidence (contracts, premium, strikes, expiries or delta exposure), attributed to a named bank, analyst, exchange or data provider, or explicitly identified as the publisher's own data. Includes a social post relaying a named source's options-flow report. Prefer this topic over market-analysis for options-flow reporting. Trade observation dates or periods may differ from publication time; missing dates must not be inferred. Not generic bullish or bearish opinions, trade recommendations, promotional unusual-activity claims without attributed figures, options education or an options-chain snapshot alone. Call buying does not establish bullish intent, opening positions or trader identity; it may reflect spreads, hedging, closing trades or dealer activity.

topics.label: market reporting and analysis
topics.description: Substantive, current financial reporting or analysis explaining today's stock, bond, currency, commodity or credit markets, sector rotations, a trading-session recap, institutional positioning, company fundamentals or valuation, or the economic implications of newly reported data. Must contain concrete market developments, figures, evidence or attributed analyst findings. Not generic stock picks, promotional investing content, evergreen personal-finance advice, speculative price predictions or an opinion without reported evidence.

topics.label: US market movers
topics.description: News that moves or is likely to move US markets: a Fed decision or Fed official signaling policy, a major US economic data release, or a foreign event with a clear, direct channel into US stocks, Treasury yields, the dollar, or oil, such as a foreign central bank (Bank of Japan, ECB, Bank of England, PBOC) deciding or signaling a rate change, a sharp yen or yuan move, Japanese or Chinese selling or buying of US assets, an OPEC output decision, or a foreign crisis markets are reacting to. Not routine foreign data or commentary that only matters to that country's own economy.

topics.label: company outlook and analyst actions
topics.description: A notable public company raising, cutting, or reaffirming guidance, issuing a profit warning, announcing a buyback or dividend change, winning or losing a material contract, or experiencing a substantial share-price move with a reported concrete catalyst. Also a named analyst or bank upgrading or downgrading a stock, changing a price target, or releasing a new quantified forecast. Not generic stock picks, evergreen investing advice, or promotional articles.

topics.label: credit and banking
topics.description: A concrete development in banking, lending, debt or credit markets: a material bond issuance or financing deal, default, bankruptcy or restructuring, credit-rating change, bank funding or liquidity issue, or newly reported changes in Treasury yields, mortgage rates, credit spreads or lending conditions. Not personal-finance advice or evergreen product comparisons.

topics.label: tariffs and trade
topics.description: A government imposing, raising, cutting, or suspending tariffs, import duties, or export controls, or countries agreeing, signing, or breaking off a trade deal. Not a single small business's experience of tariffs.

topics.label: 2026 midterms
topics.description: A concrete 2026 US midterm development: a primary or special election result, a new poll with figures, a candidate entering, dropping out, or being endorsed, a fundraising filing, or a court or election-law ruling. Not campaign-trail color or voter-mood pieces.

topics.label: AI industry and antitrust
topics.description: A concrete AI industry event (a major AI company like OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, xAI, or Meta AI releasing a model, disclosing an incident, striking a deal, or facing a lawsuit; a government passing or proposing AI regulation) or a major antitrust action against a large company. Not product explainers, workplace advice, or speculation about AI.

topics.label: major layoffs
topics.description: A company announcing or carrying out layoffs or job cuts of a specific large number of workers. Not stories about one worker's dismissal or legal case.

topics.label: M&A and public listings
topics.description: A merger, acquisition, takeover, take-private deal, spin-off, or IPO/public listing that has been announced, agreed, or completed.

topics.label: funding and valuations
topics.description: A company raising a funding round or disclosing a new valuation.

topics.label: executive changes
topics.description: A CEO, CFO, COO, CTO, president, or chair of a notable public or large private business being appointed, resigning, or ousted. Not sports clubs, teams, or athletes.

topics.label: quarterly results headlines
topics.description: A public company reporting quarterly or annual earnings results, including beats or misses versus expectations.
